metadata.title: Edge laws, a Hadamard formula and kink singularities for eigenfunctions of the localized Weil quadratic form
metadata.description: Paper (v0.2.0), with numerical supplement and the earlier research notes (v0.1.x), on the localized Weil quadratic form for the Riemann zeta function on L^2(-L, L), with the pole terms carrying any real weight. For every eigenfunction the edge traces A_+- exist; we prove the edge law psi(+-(L-r)) = A_+- (log 1/r)^(-1/2) with remainder O(l^-1), uniform on compact parameter ranges, and the second-order edge law with offset D = lambda + log 2 pi + gamma; the Hadamard formula d lambda/dL = -(A_+^2 + A_-^2) with explicit remainder for eigenvalues that are simple in their parity sector, by a two-window cross identity; a translation identity; the kink law (logarithmic singularities with explicit two-sided profile at L - log n and along chains of such shifts, dense for L > (1/2) log 6); and the first-order tail law sum_{|t_rho|>T} psi^(gamma_rho) psi^(-gamma_rho) = (A_+^2 + A_-^2)/(pi T) + O(1/(T log T)) over the zeta zeros, with the second-order per-sector term in smoothed form, unconditionally (no hypothesis on the location of the zeros). Not peer-reviewed; AI-assisted; checked by AI referee passes and by a separate AI system (OpenAI Codex, GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning effort; verdict: release as a preprint after minor fixes, which were addressed); nothing here proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. Priority: bramble_trace, rStation riemann_hypothesis paper 67 v1 (published 2026-10-27), posted earlier, with proofs reviewed only by AI agents, the existence of the edge traces, the Hadamard formula and the pure-log simplicity theorem; no priority is claimed for these. The traces, with a remainder of order l^-1 and a sketched step, had been derived in substance earlier in the mathia research notes, which also posed the question of a Hadamard law in edge stresses. Our independent proofs add a complete proof of the O(l^-1) rate, uniform on compact parameter ranges, and the explicit remainder in the Hadamard formula.
